items.title: 61426_Jacques Butler oral history interview
items.q: INTERVIEWER: Did you happen to hear Clifford Brown when he was in Paris? ... INTERVIEWEE: Well, probably, but see, I couldn't have heard them because I was working too much here.

ctx.x: And then I said, I think we'd better go up there and get my horn. She said, well, you've got a gold horn now. I said, yes, but I want that one, too. So I come -- I walks in and I'm a man, now. I walks in, he says, "Hello, boy." said, will you ask Mr. Blunt to give me my horn. I'd like to ask him something for five minutes (inaudible). He was pouring over that chick. (Inaudible). He said, you were too young, that is why. I said, too young for what? (Laughter.)

So anyway, he gives me my horn. He said, do you "Do you want to play?" I said, "No, Mr. Clifford." want to play? I said, no, Mr. Jackson said, I was resting, feeling good, (inaudible). Had my first taste of cavier.
